title: Benchmark
text:
This benchmark uses NGC1512_cube_mockGCs.fits, a mixed cube containing extended galaxy structure, compact GC-like sources, and sky contamination in the same field. The current benchmark is designed to answer two questions:

How much reconstruction quality is lost relative to PCA?
Does the mixed smooth+sparse spatial prior produce more concentrated compact components than vanilla NMF?


The benchmark uses outer-spaxel sky subtraction, weighted spatial smoothing for extended components, and sparse priors for the designated compact components.

mean_top1pct and mean_top5pct measure how much component-weight mass is carried by the brightest 1% or 5% of map pixels. Higher values indicate more concentrated maps. For the designated sparse components, the sparse_top1pct and sparse_top5pct columns isolate that concentration test.


In the current saved run, spatial NMF improves the vanilla NMF reconstruction MSE from 0.000399 to 0.000322, while increasing the designated sparse-component top-1% concentration from 0.057 to 0.113.

title: Benchmark
text:
Recommended Settings
The current benchmark run uses:

k = 8
outer-spaxel sky subtraction
lambda_smooth for spectral regularization
Gaussian spatial coupling for smooth components
sparse priors on the compact-source components

title: Benchmark
text:
Interpretation
PCA remains the strongest baseline for pure rank-(k) squared-error reconstruction, so the main question is not whether NMF beats PCA on MSE alone. The relevant question is whether spatial NMF preserves acceptable reconstruction quality while yielding cleaner and more interpretable component-weight maps.

title: Getting Started
text:
What the outputs mean

fit$spatial contains one component weight per spaxel and per component.
fit$spectra contains the recovered component spectra.
fit$reconstruction is the model approximation A %*% S.
fit$loss stores the optimization history.
fitted(fit, nx, ny) and predict(fit, type = "cube", nx, ny) reshape that reconstruction back into a cube.
residuals(fit, x = ...) returns data minus reconstruction.

title: Model
text:
SpaxNMF represents an IFU cube as a matrix (X _{}^{n p}), with one row per spaxel and one column per wavelength channel. The model seeks a low-rank non-negative factorization
\[
X \approx AS
\]
where:

(A _{}^{n k}) contains component weights for each spaxel
(S _{}^{k p}) contains the component spectra
(k) is the chosen factorization rank

A should be interpreted as a set of component-weight maps, not as chemical abundances.

title: Model

SpaxNMF represents an IFU cube as a matrix (X _{}^{n p}), with one row per spaxel and one column per wavelength channel. The model seeks a low-rank non-negative factorization
\[
X \approx AS
\]
where:

(A _{}^{n k}) contains component weights for each spaxel
(S _{}^{k p}) contains the component spectra
(k) is the chosen factorization rank

A should be interpreted as a set of component-weight maps, not as chemical abundances.

title: Model
text:
Objective Function
The current implementation minimizes
\[
\mathcal{L}(A,S)=
\|X-AS\|_F^2
+\lambda_S \|DS\|_F^2
+\sum_c \lambda_{A,c}\sum_{i,j} w_{ij}(A_{ic}-A_{jc})^2
+\sum_c \lambda_{C,c}\|A_{:,c}\|_1
\]
with Gaussian spatial couplings
\[
w_{ij} = \exp\left(-\frac{d_{ij}^2}{2\sigma^2}\right).
\]



Reconstruction term


(|X-AS|_F^2) matches the model to the observed spectra.




Spectral smoothness


(_S |DS|_F^2) penalizes channel-to-channel roughness in the recovered component spectra.




Spatial coherence


(_{A,c}) controls how strongly nearby spaxels are encouraged to carry similar weights for component (c).

title: Model
text:
Why The Spatial Term Matters
The spatial regularization does not smooth the spectra directly. It acts on the component weights in (A):
\[
\sum_{i,j} w_{ij}(A_{ic}-A_{jc})^2
\]
for each selected component (c). In practice this:

suppresses salt-and-pepper weight maps
stabilizes the decomposition under noise
encourages extended components to remain spatially coherent
leaves distant spaxels free to differ because the kernel weight decays with distance

title: Model
text:
Compact-Source Components
Selected components can also receive a sparsity prior
\[
\|A_{:,c}\|_1
\]
which is useful when a component is expected to be compact rather than smooth. This is the mechanism currently used to test GC-like components against a smooth galaxy/background decomposition.

title: Model
text:
Optimization
The torch implementation follows a simple projected-gradient strategy:

Initialize (A) and (S) randomly with positive entries.
Optimize the loss with Adam.
Clamp (A) and (S) to remain non-negative after each step.
Return spectra, component weights, and the reconstruction (AS).

title: Model
text:
Sanity Checks
The current tests enforce two baseline conditions:

setting lambda_spatial = 0 recovers the original smooth NMF objective
adding sparse priors improves recovery of compact-source components on a synthetic IFU mock

See Getting Started for code examples and Benchmark for the current real-cube test.

title: SpaxNMF
text:
Spatially aware NMF for integral-field spectroscopy




SpaxNMF fits non-negative component spectra together with component-weight maps, combining smooth spectral regularization, Gaussian spatial coupling, and optional sparse priors for compact sources.


Get Started See the Equations





\[
\mathcal{L}(A,S)=
\|X-AS\|_F^2
+\lambda_S \|DS\|_F^2
+\sum_c \lambda_{A,c}\sum_{i,j} w_{ij}(A_{ic}-A_{jc})^2
+\sum_c \lambda_{C,c}\|A_{:,c}\|_1
\]

A contains component weights, not chemical abundances. The spatial term regularizes those weights across neighboring spaxels through Gaussian kernel weights wij.

title: SpaxNMF
text:
Core Factorization



Factorization


Shared spectra, spatially varying weights

\[
X \approx AS
\]

X is the spaxel-by-wavelength matrix, A is the component-weight matrix, and S contains the component spectra.




Spatial term


Weighted coherence between neighboring spaxels

\[
w_{ij} = \exp\left(-\frac{d_{ij}^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)
\]

This term discourages noisy salt-and-pepper maps by penalizing strong changes between nearby component weights while allowing distant spaxels to decouple.

title: IFU Workflow
text:
Metadata
When the input to cube_to_matrix() is a FITS-like list object, non-image entries are carried forward as metadata. That metadata can be recovered from the fitted object or reconstructed cube with cube_metadata().
If redshift information is stored in the FITS-side metadata, it will now be preserved as metadata and can be carried into fitted and reconstructed outputs.
